final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest phenotype (escape) score and strong structural compatibility, though PLM/evolution support are modest; retained as primary candidate.
High phenotype and strong sequence plausibility, but lack of structural coverage is the main uncertainty; kept as a strong escape/fitness trade-off.
Excellent structure/PLM compatibility and moderate escape, providing a safe replication-preserving option.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 tool calls have been used; no further evidence can be gathered.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed HA globular-head residue; charge reversal likely reduces antibody recognition while electrostatics may remain tolerable. Conservative-fold risk is moderate and plausible for retained replication.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
High escape but low sequence plausibility and moderate structure compatibility; fitness risk reduces rank.
Very high escape is offset by very low sequence plausibility and lower structure compatibility, making replication loss more likely; demote below R224K.

Conservative lysine substitution at a positively charged antigenic-site residue may alter antibody contacts without large structural disruption. This balances escape potential with folding compatibility.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Solid structure and moderate sequence plausibility, but lower escape score limits its usefulness.
Phenotype is modest, but high structure and PLM compatibility indicate the mutation should preserve replication better than K187E; promote above it.

Aromatic ring kept but hydroxyl removed at an exposed epitope position, potentially reducing antibody contacts while maintaining hydrophobic packing. This conservative change should preserve overall HA stability.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Very low evolutionary support, low sequence plausibility, and low escape; not worth keeping.

rejection.reason: Very low evolutionary support, low sequence plausibility, and low escape; not worth keeping.

history.rationale: Adds a hydroxyl on an antigenic-surface aromatic residue; this can change B-cell epitope topography while remaining sterically similar. Likely compatible with folding at this exposed loop.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Poor sequence plausibility and low escape; fails both phenotype and fitness proxies.

rejection.reason: Poor sequence plausibility and low escape; fails both phenotype and fitness proxies.

history.rationale: Asparagine-to-aspartate substitution introduces a negative charge on a likely antibody-accessible loop, potentially reducing escape-relevant antibody binding. The residue change is small and often tolerated on exposed surfaces.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
High escape and very high sequence-model plausibility; no structural evidence but sequence fitness proxy is strong.
High phenotype and strong sequence-plausibility keep it second, though absence of structural coverage is a remaining uncertainty.

Conservative basic residue swap at an antigenic surface position may disrupt antibody epitope contacts while preserving charge and folding properties. This substitution is a favorable viability-escape tradeoff.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Balanced candidate with good escape, reasonable structure, and acceptable sequence plausibility.
Reasonable escape/structure balance, with lower PLM treated as a caution rather than a decisive failure.

Charge reversal at another likely exposed head residue could broaden escape; lysine at this position may be plausible in homolog variability. Structural risk is uncertain but this region is surface-accessible.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Moderate escape with good structure, but very low sequence plausibility suggests fitness risk.
Moderate escape/structure but very low PLM keeps it a lower-priority candidate.

Adds negative charge at a proximal globular-head loop residue, likely tuning antibody affinity without perturbing buried contacts. The polar-to-acidic change has moderate fitness risk but may improve escape scoring.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Excellent structural compatibility but low escape and low sequence plausibility; lower priority.
Strong structure compatibility but relatively low escape signal leaves it as a backup only.

Removes a negative charge at a surface candidate position, possibly altering antigenic recognition without drastic steric changes. Asparagine is a conservative polar replacement for aspartate on exposed loops.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
High EVEscape score and excellent structural compatibility despite low sequence-model plausibility; structure guard suggests folding retained.
No new evidence; direct escape is highest among top candidates and structure compatibility is strong, so low PLM/evolution priors do not justify moving it down.

Similar to R224K, this conservative substitution preserves the positive charge while changing a potential antibody contact side chain. It is expected to retain folding and receptor-binding robustness while adding immune-escape potential.
No new evidence yet; keep candidate.
Top PLM and structure compatibility with moderate-high escape; strongest combination of fitness proxies and escape.
Excellent structure/PLM support and moderate escape make it a safe high-confidence third.
